description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian classic known for its rich, creamy tomato-based sauce. Tender pieces of marinated chicken are simmered to perfection in a luscious gravy, offering a delightful balance of sweet and tangy flavors. This iconic dish is a comforting and satisfying meal, perfect for a special lunch or dinner.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, garam masala, salt, and lemon juice. Mix well to coat the chicken evenly. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 5-7 minutes on each side until lightly browned and cooked through. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and saute until translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the remaining ginger-garlic paste and green chilies (if using), cooking for another minute until fragrant. Add the pureed tomatoes, red chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, and salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until the oil separates from the masala.

instructions.title: Blend and Strain the Sauce
instructions.text: Add the soaked cashews and water to the tomato mixture. Bring to a simmer, then remove from heat. Let it cool slightly. Carefully transfer the mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. For a restaurant-style silky texture, strain the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot, pressing down on the solids to extract all the liquid.

instructions.title: Finish the Butter Chicken
instructions.text: Return the strained sauce to the stove over medium-low heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces, sugar, and crushed Kasuri Methi. Stir gently and simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the sauce. If the sauce is too thick, add a little more water.

instructions.title: Add Cream and Serve
instructions.text: Stir in the heavy cream and mix well. Heat through for 1-2 minutes, but do not boil after adding the cream to prevent curdling. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with naan, roti, or steamed basmati rice.

tips: Marinating the chicken for a longer duration, ideally overnight, significantly enhances its tenderness and flavor. Lemon juice helps tenderize the meat.
For an extra smooth and rich gravy, always blend the sauce base thoroughly and then strain it through a fine-mesh sieve. This removes any fibrous bits from onions or tomatoes.
Adjust the sweetness and spice level to your preference. Add more sugar for a sweeter taste or a pinch more red chili powder for extra heat. A dash of honey can also be used instead of sugar.
article:
Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: Your Guide to a Legendary Indian Lunch

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani as it's known in Hindi, stands as a testament to the rich culinary heritage of India. This iconic dish, with its creamy texture, smoky chicken, and vibrant tomato-based gravy, has captivated palates worldwide. Originating from Delhi in the mid-20th century, it quickly rose to prominence as a staple in Indian restaurants and homes alike. Perfect for a hearty lunch, a comforting dinner, or a special occasion, Butter Chicken offers a symphony of flavors that is both luxurious and deeply satisfying. If you've ever dreamt of recreating this restaurant-quality dish in your own kitchen, you've come to the right place. This comprehensive guide will walk you through everything you need to know to master the art of Murgh Makhani, ensuring a delicious and authentic experience.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Murgh Makhani literally translates to "chicken with butter," a name that perfectly encapsulates the essence of this beloved dish. At its core, Butter Chicken features succulent pieces of boneless chicken, traditionally marinated in yogurt and spices, then grilled or pan-fried until tender and slightly charred. This cooked chicken is then simmered in a rich, velvety gravy made primarily from tomatoes, butter, cream, and a blend of aromatic spices like ginger, garlic, garam masala, cumin, and fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi). The distinct sweetness comes from tomatoes, often balanced with a touch of sugar or honey, while the cream and butter contribute to its signature smooth, indulgent mouthfeel. It's a dish celebrated for its milder spice profile compared to some other Indian curries, making it a universally appealing choice that embodies comfort and elegance.

## Ingredients You Need for Butter Chicken

Crafting the perfect Butter Chicken requires a combination of fresh ingredients and essential spices. Here’s a breakdown of what you’ll need for a truly authentic Murgh Makhani:

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   Salt to taste
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice

For the Makhani Gravy:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   2 large onions, finely chopped or pureed
*   2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste
*   1 kg ripe tomatoes, pureed or 2 cans (400g each) crushed tomatoes
*   1/2 cup cashew nuts, soaked in warm water for 15 minutes (for creaminess)
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 tablespoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream
*   1 tablespoon honey or sugar (to balance acidity)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions to Make Butter Chicken

Follow these detailed steps to create a show-stopping Butter Chicken at home:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for best results.

2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat a grill pan, heavy-bottomed skillet, or oven to medium-high. Add a little oil. Place the marinated chicken pieces on the pan or baking sheet. Cook until they are browned and cooked through, with a slight char on the edges (this adds a wonderful smoky flavor, mimicking a tandoor). Set aside.

3.  **Prepare the Gravy Base:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt 1 tablespoon of butter with 1 tablespoon of oil over medium heat. Add the chopped or pureed onions and sauté until translucent and lightly golden, about 8-10 minutes.

4.  **Aromatic Infusion:** Add the ginger-garlic paste to the pot and cook for another 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Stir in the red chili powder, turmeric powder, and garam masala. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, to bloom the spices.

5.  **Build the Gravy:** Pour in the tomato puree or crushed tomatoes. Add the soaked and pureed cashews (blend cashews with a little water until smooth). Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have broken down and the oil starts to separate.

6.  **Smooth the Gravy:** For an extra smooth restaurant-style gravy, let the mixture cool slightly, then carefully blend it using an immersion blender or transfer to a regular blender. Blend until completely smooth. Strain the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pot to remove any remaining solids, ensuring a silky texture. This step is crucial for authentic Butter Chicken.

7.  **Combine and Simmer:** Return the smooth gravy to the pot over medium-low heat. Stir in the cooked chicken pieces, kasoori methi, honey or sugar, and salt to taste. Simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the rich gravy.

8.  **Finishing Touches:** Turn off the heat. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter and the heavy cream. Mix gently until fully incorporated. Do not boil after adding the cream, as it can curdle.

9.  **Garnish and Serve:** Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Your homemade Butter Chicken is now ready to be enjoyed!

## Pro Tips for the Best Butter Chicken Results

Achieving truly exceptional Butter Chicken involves more than just following a recipe. Here are some pro tips to elevate your Murgh Makhani:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is ideal.
*   **Charred Chicken for Depth:** The slight char on the chicken pieces from grilling or pan-frying adds an invaluable smoky depth that is characteristic of authentic Butter Chicken. Don't just boil or bake the chicken plain.
*   **The Power of Kasoori Methi:** Kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves) is non-negotiable. Crush it between your palms before adding it to release its unique aroma and slightly bitter, earthy flavor, which is essential to the dish.
*   **Blend and Strain for Silkiness:** For that signature smooth, luxurious gravy, blending and then straining the tomato-cashew base is a game-changer. It removes any fibrous bits and ensures a restaurant-quality texture.
*   **Balance Flavors:** Taste your gravy before the final steps. Adjust salt, sugar/honey (to balance tomato acidity), and chili powder to your preference. A perfectly balanced Butter Chicken is sweet, tangy, and subtly spicy.
*   **High-Quality Dairy:** Use good quality butter and heavy cream. They are fundamental to the richness and flavor of Murgh Makhani.

## Serving Suggestions for Murgh Makhani

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments, making it a perfect Indian lunch recipe. Here are some classic serving suggestions:

*   **Naan Bread:** Soft, pillowy naan is the quintessential partner, perfect for scooping up every last drop of the luscious gravy. Garlic naan or butter naan adds an extra layer of flavor.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a neutral canvas that allows the rich flavors of the Murgh Makhani to shine.
*   **Roti or Chapati:** For a lighter option, whole wheat roti or chapati also works beautifully.
*   **Raita:** A cooling cucumber raita or plain yogurt can offer a refreshing contrast to the richness of the curry.
*   **Onion Salad:** A simple kachumber salad (diced onion, cucumber, tomato with lemon and salt) or just sliced raw onions with a squeeze of lime provides a fresh crunch.

## Variations and Substitutions for Butter Chicken

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is divine, you can easily adapt it to suit dietary needs or personal preferences:

*   **Vegetarian Butter "Chicken":** Replace chicken with paneer (Indian cheese), firm tofu, or even chickpeas and cauliflower for a delicious vegetarian version. Marinate paneer or tofu similarly and pan-fry until golden.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to make it milder or spicier. For a vibrant red color without too much heat, use Kashmiri chili powder.
*   **Dairy-Free Option:** For a dairy-free Murgh Makhani, use plant-based yogurt for marination, coconut oil instead of butter, and full-fat coconut milk or cashew cream instead of heavy cream. Ensure to use a dairy-free butter substitute.
*   **Smoky Flavor without a Grill:** If you don't have a grill, you can achieve a smoky flavor by placing a small, red-hot charcoal piece in a small bowl within the curry, drizzling a little oil or ghee over it, and covering the pot for a few minutes. This is called "dhungar" method.
*   **No Cashews:** If you have a nut allergy or don't have cashews, you can use blanched almonds or skip them and rely more on the cream for richness, though the texture will be slightly different.

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is more than just a dish; it's an experience. With this detailed guide, you're now equipped to bring the magic of this legendary Indian curry into your own home. Gather your ingredients, follow the steps, and prepare to impress your taste buds with a truly unforgettable meal. Enjoy the process, and savor every creamy, flavorful bite!
